title: UN Palestinian Rights Committee Formally Condemns Khan al-Ahmar Eviction Order as War Crime
detail: The Bureau of the UN Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People (CEIRPP) issued a formal condemnation on June 4, 2026 of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's order to evict and demolish Khan al-Ahmar — a Bedouin village of approximately 300 people in the E1 area east of Jerusalem. The UN stated the eviction constitutes forced transfer of civilians and is a war crime under international law, reiterating demands to halt the E1 settlement plan which, if implemented, would sever Palestinian territorial contiguity between the northern and southern West Bank. Separately, OHCHR reiterated its demand that Israel halt forcible displacement and settlement expansion in the E1 corridor. The order was issued by Smotrich on May 19, 2026 — the same day he announced the ICC had sought an arrest warrant against him — and is seen as retaliatory defiance of international legal pressure. Khan al-Ahmar has been under Israeli demolition orders since 2011; the ICJ ordered Israel to halt demolition in 2019. Execution of the eviction order would trigger the most significant E1 settlement advance in years and is opposed by the EU, US State Department, and all permanent UNSC members.

media.caption: UN condemns Khan al-Ahmar eviction order as war crime; OHCHR demands halt to E1 settlement expansion — June 4, 2026

title: At Least 10 Palestinians Killed in IDF Strikes Across Gaza; US Embassy Issues Security Advisory
detail: At least 10 Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza on June 4, 2026, per multiple reports. The US Embassy in Jerusalem simultaneously issued a security advisory warning US citizens of a 'complex' security environment across Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza — reflecting elevated tension in the region. The embassy advisory came against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Israel war against Iran, the stalled Gaza Phase 2 negotiations, and near-daily Israeli strikes within the October 2025 ceasefire framework that have now killed more than 940 Palestinians since October 11, 2025. Israeli operations continued despite the formal ceasefire structure, with the IDF citing ongoing Hamas armed activity and operational threats.

media.caption: At least 10 Palestinians killed in IDF strikes; US Embassy issues security advisory for Israel, West Bank, Gaza — June 4, 2026

title: Netanyahu Confirms Heated Call with Trump, Insists They Agree on 'Main Things'
detail: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed in an interview on June 4, 2026 that he had a heated conversation with US President Donald Trump — publicly acknowledging the tense exchange first reported June 2 regarding a planned Israeli strike on Hezbollah targets in Beirut. Netanyahu downplayed the rift, insisting that he and Trump agree on 'the main things' and that the disagreement was tactical rather than strategic. The episode — in which Trump urged Netanyahu not to strike Beirut — reflects ongoing divergence between Washington's desire to contain regional escalation (particularly as the US remains engaged in direct military operations against Iran) and Israel's posture of proactive deterrence against the full Iran-aligned Axis of Resistance. Israel agreed to defer the strike provided it was not attacked first.

media.caption: Netanyahu confirms heated Trump call, says both agree on 'main things' — June 4, 2026
